core_problem: High memory consumption in 3D-CNNs for brain tumor segmentation in 3D MRIs, and the lack of uncertainty information in most existing methods, which is critical for medical diagnosis.
methodology_summary: Proposes a 3D encoder-decoder architecture based on V-Net [6], trained with patching techniques to reduce memory consumption and handle unbalanced data. Introduces voxel-wise uncertainty (epistemic and aleatoric) using test-time dropout and data-augmentation, respectively.
datasets_eval: Brain Tumor Segmentation (BraTS) challenge (started in 2012), specifically mentioning BraTS 2020 training.
empirical_results: Best results obtained with the V-Net model directly when post-processing is applied. Dice score and Hausdorff distance showed lower performance on the validation set, especially in the ET region.
explicit_limitations: Entropy provides a global measure instead of a map for sub-regions, necessitating the use of voxel-wise uncertainty.
pipeline_steps: used to assess the diagnosis, treatment and evaluation of the disease.
